title: NVDM 1.1 scope registry entry
description: One entry of schemas/nvdm/scopes.json (schemas/nvdm/RULES.md Part 4). The vocabularies are closed: appending a ref system, level or relation type is a one-line MINOR change, made when the first entry needs it. Graph rules (targets registered, administrative-parent acyclic, one country per place, method and evidence on every intersects) are enforced by scripts/validate_nvdm.py (spec 4.7).

kind.description: What the scope is; an artifact's scope.kind must equal it (spec 4.1).

name.description: Display name. It may change; the id may not.

refs.description: The scope's identities in external systems (spec 4.4).

relations.description: Typed links to other registered scopes (spec 4.5).

ref.description: A namespaced external identity (spec 4.4). A code is never guessed: it is read from a file already in the repo or verified at its publisher.

system.description: The external identifier system. lgd is India's Local Government Directory; census-2011 is the Census of India 2011.

level.description: The administrative level the code identifies in that system.

code.description: The identifier, as a string. One system and code pair belongs to one scope.

as_of.description: Source vintage of the code, where known.

type.description: administrative-parent: place to parent place. intersects: water system to a place it crosses, geometry only, never supply or entitlement. projection-of: an administrative view to its canonical water system (the registry form of the envelope's projection.of). See spec 4.5.

target.description: The id of another registered scope.

method.description: How the relation was established (spec 4.5). Required, with evidence, on every intersects (enforced by scripts/validate_nvdm.py). geometry: the system's geometry in the repo was tested against the place's polygon. published: the source's publisher states it. crosswalk: joined through an identifier. manual: a reviewed mapping.

evidence.description: A repo path or URL that lets the relation be re-checked: for geometry, the boundary or centerline that was tested.
